cues.en: Instructor: In this video, I'm going to introduce you to the concept of statistical moments.
cues.zh: 這部影片介紹統計動差。

cues.en: It turns out that you already know several of these statistical moments, even if you didn't know what they were called.
cues.zh: 其實你已知道其中幾個，即使不知道名字。

cues.en: Statistical moments is a concept that brings together a lot of different kinds of descriptive statistics under one general mathematical framework.
cues.zh: 統計動差這個概念，把很多敘述統計，放進通用的數學架構。

cues.en: So what are statistical moments?
cues.zh: 什麼是統計動差？

cues.en: Well, first of all, they have nothing to do with this kind of a moment, a piece in time.
cues.zh: 首先，與時間中的moment、片刻，毫無關係。

cues.en: Maybe you remember that weird song from the '80s, I think it was, it was, "give me one moment in time."
cues.zh: 也許記得八○年代那首奇怪的歌，我想是，唱著「給我一個時間中的片刻」。

cues.en: Nothing to do with that.
cues.zh: 與那無關。

cues.en: I don't really know why they're called moments.
cues.zh: 其實不知道為何叫moments。

cues.en: It's probably some older use of the English word moment.
cues.zh: 大概是moment這個英文字的古老用法。

cues.en: But anyway, there is a kind of general formula that gets a little bit adapted for each specific moment, but the general formula looks something like this.
cues.zh: 總之，有個一般公式，各階動差稍作調整，但大致像這樣。

cues.en: So we have the kth moment of a data set of a distribution, and that is defined as 1 over N times the sum
cues.zh: 分布、資料集的第k階動差，定義為1/N乘以總和，

cues.en: over all of the N data points of the difference between each individual data point and the average over all the data points and then this raised to the kth power.
cues.zh: 對N個資料點，各點減全體平均，再取k次方後加總。

cues.en: So that is the general formula for a statistical moment.
cues.zh: 這是統計動差的一般公式。

cues.en: Now you this should already look familiar, this formula.
cues.zh: 這應該已很熟悉。

cues.en: So we have seen that the average value looks like this.
cues.zh: 之前看過平均值像這樣。

cues.en: This is the formula for computing the average, and this is actually the first moment of a dataset or of a distribution.
cues.zh: 這是平均公式，其實是資料集或分布的一階動差。

cues.en: The first moment of a distribution is the mean, it's the average value.
cues.zh: 分布的一階動差，就是平均值。

cues.en: Now you can see here, so setting K to be one, then K to be one, which means you drop this exponent altogether, and then it really doesn't make sense
cues.zh: 這裡設k=1，也就是去掉指數，這時其實不應該，

cues.en: to subtract the mean because then the values are always going to be zero.
cues.zh: 減平均，因為值永遠會是0。

cues.en: Even if the mean isn't zero, this number will return zero, this formula will return zero if we're subtracting the average value here.
cues.zh: 即使平均不為0，只要這裡減去平均，公式都回傳0。

cues.en: So that's the first moment.
cues.zh: 這是一階動差。

cues.en: And then we get to the second moment, and this is the familiar variance computation.
cues.zh: 再來二階動差，熟悉的變異數計算。

cues.en: This you've seen plenty of times before, including exactly this formula.
cues.zh: 已看過很多次，包含完全相同公式。

cues.en: So the second moment is the difference between all the individual data values and the mean and then you square those differences,
cues.zh: 第二階動差，是計算每個資料值與平均值之差，再將這些差平方，

cues.en: sum them up and divide by N So that is the variance.
cues.zh: 加總、除N，就是變異數。

cues.en: Now, we could go on to the third moment and the fourth moment, they look exactly like this.
cues.zh: 接著三階、四階，看起來也像這樣。

cues.en: These are called unstandardized statistical moments.
cues.zh: 這些叫未標準化統計動差。

cues.en: And it turns out that what we actually use in practice is called the standardized statistical moments.
cues.zh: 實務上，使用的是標準化統計動差。

cues.en: Now, I'm going to walk you through the first four statistical moments because these are the ones that are most often studied and used in practice.
cues.zh: 會帶你看前四階，因為它們最常研究、最常用。

cues.en: So the first statistical moment is the average value.
cues.zh: 第一階是平均值。

cues.en: The second one is the variance.
cues.zh: 第二階是變異數。

cues.en: That's the dispersion around the mean.
cues.zh: 也就是平均周圍的離散程度。

cues.en: The third statistical moment is called skewness.
cues.zh: 第三階叫偏度。

cues.en: That's related to dispersion asymmetry.
cues.zh: 與離散程度的不對稱有關。

cues.en: I'm gonna have a slide just about this.
cues.zh: 有一張投影片專門談。

cues.en: I also have a slide about this, this is kurtosis, that's the fourth moment, and that's like the fatness of the tails of the distribution.
cues.zh: 也有一張談峰度，也就是第四階，像分布尾巴的厚度。

cues.en: And what you can see is that the general formula appears in all of these cases and what we're adding is some additional variance terms in here
cues.zh: 一般公式出現在所有情況，另外加入一些變異數項，

cues.en: that are essentially scaling these quantities down so they don't grow really, really large.
cues.zh: 基本上把這些量縮放，避免非常大。

cues.en: You can imagine these numbers are gonna start getting pretty big once you multiply or raise to higher and higher powers.
cues.zh: 可以想像，乘上或取越高次方，數字越大。

cues.en: So that's kind of the purpose of these standardization factors that basically just allows us to look at skewness and kurtosis without these numbers
cues.zh: 這些標準化因子，就是讓我們看偏度與峰度時，數字不會，

cues.en: just getting really, really big.
cues.zh: 變得非常巨大。

cues.en: Okay, so now these are just the formulas.
cues.zh: 以上是公式。

cues.en: Let me spend a slide talking about each one.
cues.zh: 各花一張投影片談。

cues.en: Okay, so I actually don't really need to talk about the first moment.
cues.zh: 其實一階不用再說。

cues.en: You already know this.
cues.zh: 已經知道。

cues.en: It's the average value.
cues.zh: 就是平均值。

cues.en: It's the dominant measure of the central tendency of a distribution.
cues.zh: 最主要的集中趨勢量。

cues.en: So first moment is the mean.
cues.zh: 所以一階動差是平均。

cues.en: Second moment is the variance or the dispersion around the mean.
cues.zh: 二階是變異數、平均周圍的離散程度。

cues.en: Nothing particularly new to say here.
cues.zh: 沒有特別新的內容。

cues.en: Just to commit to memory that the second statistical moment of a distribution is the variance.
cues.zh: 只要記住，分布二階統計動差是變異數。

cues.en: Okay, and then we get to the third moment, and that is the skew or the skewness.
cues.zh: 第三階，是偏斜、偏度。

cues.en: Now, I've mentioned this term skew already a few times in this course, but I didn't really define it, so here's what the skew refers to.
cues.zh: 課程已提過幾次，但沒真正定義，現在說明。

cues.en: When you have a distribution that's kind of pulled off in one direction like this or like this, that indicates a skew.
cues.zh: 分布像這樣，被拉向某方向，就表示偏斜。

cues.en: This is what skew means.
cues.zh: 這就是偏斜的意思。

cues.en: Now you can see we can have the high clustering here to the left, or we can have the high clustering here to the right, and this would be called positive skew or right skew
cues.zh: 這裡大量聚左，這裡聚右。這種叫正偏、右偏。

cues.en: So the direction of the skew refers to where you're pulling the values off into the range of outliers.
cues.zh: 偏斜方向，是指數值被拉向離群範圍的方向。

cues.en: So we're pulling off the values from the right.
cues.zh: 這裡往右拉。

cues.en: So therefore we have a right skew or a positive skew.
cues.zh: 所以右偏、正偏。

cues.en: Here we are pulling off the values to the left, so we have left skew.
cues.zh: 這裡往左拉，所以左偏。

cues.en: It's also called negative skew.
cues.zh: 也叫負偏。

cues.en: So third moment is the measure of skewness and skewness refers to the asymmetry in the dispersion around the mean, around the center of the data.
cues.zh: 三階動差衡量偏度，也就是平均、資料中心周圍離散的不對稱。

cues.en: Okay, so that's the third moment.
cues.zh: 這是三階。

cues.en: And then we have the fourth moment, and that is kurtosis, and that's defined as the fatness of the tail.
cues.zh: 第四階是峰度，定義為尾巴厚度。

cues.en: So let me give you two examples.
cues.zh: 給兩個例子。

cues.en: Here we see distributions that kind of look a bit Gaussian, they're symmetric, so the skew would actually be very small.
cues.zh: 分布有點像高斯，而且對稱，所以偏度很小。

cues.en: But neither of these looks really exactly like a Gaussian.
cues.zh: 但都不完全像高斯。

cues.en: This one actually slopes down too slowly for a Gaussian, although it does eventually get down very close to zero here, but this would have a high kurtosis,
cues.zh: 這個相較高斯下降太慢，雖然最終非常接近0，但峰度高；

cues.en: and this distribution falls off too quickly relative to a Gaussian, so this has low kurtosis.
cues.zh: 這個下降比高斯快，所以峰度低。

cues.en: So high kurtosis means it's wider, it's more distributed compared to a Gaussian, low kurtosis means that that the tails are shorter
cues.zh: 高峰度表示比高斯更寬、更分散；低峰度表示尾巴更短，

cues.en: than what you would expect for a Gaussian.
cues.zh: 相較高斯的預期。

cues.en: Sometimes you also see these high kurtosis distributions never really getting to zero.
cues.zh: 有時高峰度分布，也似乎永遠不到0。

cues.en: So I could have drawn this with these distributions, you know, these side lobes here, these tails basically flatlining around here, kind of ascent toting around here.
cues.zh: 可以把它畫成兩邊的尾巴，大致在這裡變平，漸近這裡。

cues.en: That would also be an example of high kurtosis.
cues.zh: 這也是高峰度例子。

cues.en: So kurtosis is really all about the tails and whether the tails are bigger than what you would expect for a Gaussian or smaller than what you would expect for a Gaussian.
cues.zh: 峰度就是看尾巴，比高斯預期更大，還是更小。

cues.en: Alright, so those are the formulas and those are the pictures.
cues.zh: 以上是公式與圖像。

cues.en: What I've done in this slide is kind of organize everything together.
cues.zh: 這張投影片，把所有內容整理在一起。

cues.en: This, I think is worth committing to memory, this table.
cues.zh: 這張表值得記住。

cues.en: So if you like, you can take a screenshot of this slide.
cues.zh: 可以截圖。

cues.en: This is worth memorizing.
cues.zh: 值得背。

cues.en: The first moment is the mean, it's the average value, and it's like the center of gravity here.
cues.zh: 一階是平均值，像重心。

cues.en: The second moment is the variance.
cues.zh: 二階是變異數。

cues.en: It's a measure of dispersion around the mean.
cues.zh: 衡量平均周圍的離散程度。

cues.en: The third moment is the skewness, and it measures the asymmetry of the dispersion, either to the right or to the left.
cues.zh: 三階是偏度，衡量離散的不對稱，向右或向左。

cues.en: And the fourth moment is called kurtosis, and it measures the fatness of the tails, and we say that there's a distribution as high kurtosis if the tails are higher than what you would expect
cues.zh: 第四階動差稱為峰度，衡量尾端的厚度；如果尾端比預期更高，我們就說這個分布有高峰度，

cues.en: for Gaussian and low kurtosis or small kurtosis if the tails are smaller than what you would expect for a Gaussian.
cues.zh: 比較基準是高斯分布；如果尾端比高斯分布預期的更小，就稱為低峰度或較小的峰度。

cues.en: So those are the main four statistical moments that appear most often.
cues.zh: 這是最常見的四個主要統計動差。

cues.en: Obviously, they go higher.
cues.zh: 當然還能更高階。

cues.en: You can have a fifth statistical moment, a sixth statistical moment, and so on.
cues.zh: 可以有五階、六階，依此類推。

cues.en: But I don't know if I've ever seen any applications of such high statistical moments.
cues.zh: 但不知道是否看過這麼高階的應用。

cues.en: Certainly, the fourth statist statistical moment is used, kurtosis is used.
cues.zh: 四階統計動差、峰度，當然有人用。

cues.en: It's one of the dominant ways of computing something called an independent components analysis, or ICA.
cues.zh: 它是計算獨立成分分析，也就是ICA的主要方法之一。

cues.en: I'm actually gonna introduce you to ICA in the future towards the end of this course.
cues.zh: 課程後段，也會介紹ICA。
